phase1_decomposition.property_under_test: PROP-W1B10-48: versioned_hashes array correctly computed from blob KZG commitments via kzg_commitment_to_versioned_hash
phase1_decomposition.el_scope_analysis: The CL-side computation (kzg_commitment_to_versioned_hash function, NewPayloadRequest population) is NOT implemented in this EL codebase. The EL receives versioned_hashes as a sidecar field from the CL via the Engine API. However, the EL DOES validate that the received versioned_hashes match the blob versioned hashes embedded in blob transactions within the block.
invariants_tested: INV-1: Number of sidecar versioned_hashes == number of blob versioned hashes in block body transactions

audit_items.title: Verify CL-to-EL Trust Boundary: Does the Execution Engine properly validate versioned_hashes received from Consensus Layer?

code_scope.component: Execution Layer - Cancun Payload Validation

phase1_decomposition.property_under_test: PROP-W1B10-48: Does the Execution Engine properly validate versioned_hashes received from Consensus Layer?
invariants_tested: INV-1: EL independently validates CL-provided versioned_hashes by comparing against blob transaction data in block body
INV-2: EL returns INVALID PayloadStatus when versioned_hashes mismatch
INV-3: EL returns latestValidHash: null for versioned hash validation failures (per Engine API spec)
INV-4: No implicit trust - EL does NOT blindly accept CL-provided versioned_hashes
code_flow: 1. engine_newPayloadV3 receives (payload, versioned_hashes, parent_beacon_block_root) from CL
2. Wraps into ExecutionData with CancunPayloadFields sidecar containing versioned_hashes
4. Engine tree calls ensure_well_formed_payload which delegates to cancun::ensure_well_formed_fields
6. On failure: PayloadError::InvalidVersionedHashes -> is_invalid_versioned_hashes() -> latestValidHash: null
phase1_decomposition.trust_boundary_analysis: The EL does NOT blindly trust CL-provided versioned_hashes. It independently extracts blob versioned hashes from block body transactions and performs a strict comparison. This is the correct trust model per Engine API specification.

phase2_verification.methodology: Full code path tracing from Engine API entry to validation logic

findings.description: EL independently validates versioned_hashes against block body blob transactions. No implicit trust vulnerability.
findings.evidence: cancun.rs:93-120 - ensure_matching_blob_versioned_hashes extracts hashes from block body via blob_versioned_hashes_iter() and compares against sidecar.

findings.description: Validation failure returns INVALID status with latestValidHash: null per Engine API spec.
findings.evidence: tree/mod.rs:2560 - is_invalid_versioned_hashes() check returns None for latest_valid_hash. PayloadError::InvalidVersionedHashes is mapped correctly.

findings.description: Validation runs immediately, even during active sync, per Engine API requirement.
findings.evidence: tree/mod.rs:538 comment: 'This validation MUST be instantly run in all cases even during active sync process.' The validation is called in ensure_well_formed_payload before any state access.

findings.description: Both V3 and V4 engine_newPayload endpoints include versioned_hashes in sidecar and route through the same validation path.
findings.evidence: engine_api.rs:873-916 - Both new_payload_v3 and new_payload_v4 construct CancunPayloadFields with versioned_hashes and call metered variants that route through ensure_well_formed_payload.

phase3_classification.residual_risk: None identified. The EL correctly implements the Engine API versioned_hashes validation per spec. No timing side-channels were identified in the hash comparison (standard iterator-based comparison, not constant-time, but this is non-sensitive data comparison per spec).

invariants_tested: INV-2: For each i: versioned_hashes[i] == blob_tx_versioned_hash[i] [element-wise binding]

code_flow: 1. ensure_matching_blob_versioned_hashes counts blob versioned hashes from block body
3. If lengths match, uses zip to compare element-by-element

phase2_verification.methodology: Structural code review with edge case analysis

findings.description: Length invariant (len(versioned_hashes) == len(blob_commitments)) enforced at cancun.rs:100.
findings.evidence: Line 100: `if num_blob_versioned_hashes != versioned_hashes.len()` - returns error before any iteration.

findings.description: Element-wise binding correctly implemented via zip after length check. No off-by-one possible since zip stops at shorter iterator (both same length).
findings.evidence: Lines 105-111: zip iteration with element comparison. Length already verified equal.

findings.description: Zero blobs edge case: When no sidecar and no blob txs, num_blob_versioned_hashes==0 and cancun_sidecar_fields is None, the else branch check `if num_blob_versioned_hashes > 0` is false, so Ok(()) is returned. Correct.
findings.evidence: Lines 112-116: Only returns error when blob hashes exist without sidecar.

findings.description: Max blobs handling: No explicit max blob count check in this function. The MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK limit is enforced at higher levels (blob gas used validation in validate_cancun_gas). This function handles arbitrary-length arrays correctly.
findings.evidence: The iteration is O(n) with no overflow risk since it's comparing existing arrays.

findings.description: The EL validates versioned_hashes match blob transaction data, but the cryptographic binding (SHA256 hash of KZG commitment with version byte prefix) happens at the alloy/revm level, not in this validation code. The EL trusts that blob transactions already contain correctly computed versioned hashes per EIP-4844 transaction validation.
findings.evidence: The blob_versioned_hashes field in EIP-4844 transactions is validated during transaction validation (signature recovery, type checks) before reaching this payload validation.

phase3_classification.scope_limitation: The cryptographic hash computation (SHA256 of KZG commitment) is delegated to the alloy/revm crate and was not audited in this check.
phase3_classification.residual_risk: None identified in the EL validation logic. The binding between versioned_hashes (from CL) and blob transaction hashes (from block body) is correctly enforced.
